title: Data Quality Audit
description: Audits experiments and artifacts for missing metadata, calibration records, provenance and traceability gaps, and raw-data retention.

steps.prompt: Audit the experiments and artifacts for completeness of metadata. Check whether each record includes: operator name, timestamp, instrument ID, sample ID, electrolyte batch, temperature, and protocol version. Use this rubric — 1: all fields present across all records; 2: 1-2 minor fields missing in a few records; 3: a core field (e.g. sample ID or temperature) missing in some records; 4: systematic metadata gaps across multiple experiments; 5: metadata so incomplete that records cannot be linked to samples or conditions. Cite specific experiment IDs or artifact names where gaps are found. List 3-5 mitigations.

Evaluate whether instrument calibration records are present and current for the experiments in context. Consider: potentiostat calibration dates, reference electrode replacement/reconditioning logs, balance and volumetric calibration, and temperature probe verification. Use this rubric — 1: all instruments calibrated within stated intervals, records attached; 2: minor gap (one instrument overdue, low impact); 3: a key instrument (e.g. reference electrode) lacks recent calibration, data uncertainty elevated; 4: multiple instruments without calibration records, quantitative results unreliable; 5: no calibration documentation exists for this dataset. Cite specific instruments or experiment dates from the context. Provide 3-5 mitigations.

Assess whether the chain of custody and data provenance is intact from raw measurement to reported result. Consider: whether raw data files are linked to processed results, whether sample preparation steps are traceable to source materials, whether any data transformation steps are documented, and whether version control is used for analysis scripts or processed files. Use this rubric — 1: full provenance chain, raw files archived and linked; 2: minor gap (one transformation undocumented); 3: processed results present but raw files missing or unlinked for some experiments; 4: significant provenance break, cannot reconstruct how results were obtained; 5: no traceability from source data to reported values. Cite specific artifacts or page notes. List 3-5 targeted mitigations.

Determine whether raw data is being retained in a durable, accessible form. Look for: raw instrument output files attached as artifacts, whether only processed summaries exist, whether data is stored in a version-controlled or backed-up location, and whether retention is consistent across experiments. Use this rubric — 1: all raw files attached and backed up; 2: most raw files present, a few missing; 3: raw files present for recent work only, older experiments have summaries only; 4: raw files rarely attached, only processed values retained; 5: no raw data retained, results cannot be reanalyzed. Cite specific examples from the artifacts in context. Provide 3-5 mitigations.
